newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan sets reform income tax at 25 pct - official.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sets reform income tax at 25 pct - official.

text.p: Taiwan will maintain its business income tax at 25 percent in a reform merging the island's two income taxes, junking a drive to set the combined tax at 35 percent, a Finance Ministry official said on Thursday.

The package merging the business income tax and personal income tax -- including a final fixing of the combined tax rate -- would not be made final until October 11, the official said by telephone on condition his name not be used.
A formal announcement would be made on that date, he said.
Objections from various business associations forced the ministry to compromise on the overall post-reform tax level, the official told Reuters.
The ministry had hoped for a merged tax rate of 35 percent.

Enforcing the combined business income tax at 25 percent would mean an annual reduction in government tax revenues of more than T$20 billion, forcing the Finance Ministry to scrable for other income, the official said.
If the tax is fixed at 25 percent "we will find some way to balance the loss", he said. He declined to elaborate.
Local newspapers had reported that raising the merged business income tax to 35 percent would generate an annual tax windfall of T$11 billion.

In June, the ministry appointed a commission to study ways of reforming the income tax in Taiwan's drive to liberalise its financial markets. The commission started work on July 1, aiming to complete a feasibility study within four months.

Business leaders have complained tha Taiwan's system of dual income taxes, where earnings are subject to a business income tax and a personal income tax, was cumbersome and unfair. The commission of scholars, industry leaders and officials also is looking at ways to streamline tariffs, business taxes on financial and insurance operations, and commodities taxes.
